messages.subject: The same likelihood
parts:
Hello, I have a small sample size and got some "crazy" results...
Is it possible that user model and restricted model have the same likelihood? Is it possible that it is positive?
The funny thing is the coefficients seem to make sense... but can I trust this estimation with all
the crazy stuff above?
Thanks a lot
Niv

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: The same likelihood
parts:
On 01/05/2016 06:17 AM, niv de malach wrote:
> Hello, I have a small sample size and got some "crazy" results...

> Degrees of freedom 0

You have fitted a saturated model, with df = 0. There were no
restrictions, so the likelihood of H0 and H1 must be the same.

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: The same likelihood
parts: how come 40 observation and 6 parameter estimates (a1-a6) lead to a saturated model ?

N = 40 determines the width of your SEs, but not your df.  The "observations" in (means and) covariance structure analysis are the nonredundant elements of the (mean vector and) covariance matrix.

Terry
